definitions.explanation: The quality of understanding and caring about others' feelings and needs. Being able to put oneself in another's position and act accordingly.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}いやりのある{人|ひと}になりたい。
examples.english: I want to be a considerate person.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{思|おも}いやりに{感動|かんどう}した。
examples.english: I was moved by his thoughtfulness.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}いやりを{持|も}って{接|せっ}することが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to treat people with consideration.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{思|おも}いやりのある{人|ひと} (a considerate/thoughtful person)
・{思|おも}いやりを{持|も}つ (to have consideration)
・{思|おも}いやりに{欠|か}ける (to lack consideration)
・{思|おも}いやりの{心|こころ} (a caring heart)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{思|おも}いやり is an important Japanese cultural value, emphasizing anticipating others' needs without being asked. It's related to concepts like {気配|きくば}り (attentiveness) and {心遣|こころづか}い (consideration).

ETYMOLOGY:
From {思|おも}いやる (to sympathize with, to consider) - literally "to send one's thoughts" to another person.

RELATED WORDS:
・{気配|きくば}り (attentiveness, being considerate)
・{心遣|こころづか}い (consideration, thoughtfulness)
・{優|やさ}しさ (kindness, gentleness)
